key_insight: A two-stage Mamba sequence model can read superconducting qubit signals more accurately and efficiently than prior ML-based readout methods, while directly correcting relaxation-induced errors.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a faster, lower-parameter path to robust frequency-multiplexed qubit readout, which is important for scalable fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Stage 1: initial qubit state discrimination from readout traces
Stage 2: refinement to detect and mitigate relaxation errors
Uses Mamba for linear-complexity sequence modeling instead of large FNNs
evidence_signal: The best lightweight model achieved a geometric mean readout fidelity of 0.906 and the optimal model reached 0.911, with 49.6% fewer parameters and 0.893 fidelity at 500 ns readout duration.
watch_item: Performance is reported on readout traces from a specific superconducting-qubit setting, so robustness across different hardware, noise regimes, and calibration drift still needs validation.
paper_title: Multi-Stage Mamba-Based Architecture for Fast and Scalable Superconducting Qubit Readout
